card.name: Right before a journal or publication name
card.fires_on: Punctuation or small words in citations just before the name of the journal, periodical or publisher is given. Also verbs like 'appeared' or 'filed a' that lead into where something was published.

modes.label: Citation punctuation
modes.description: A period, quote mark or comma closing an article title or edition, right before the journal name.
modes.example: Race, the Public Sphere, and Abolition in Late Eighteenth-century New York<<.">> Journal of the Early Republic (20

modes.label: Appeared in phrasing
modes.description: Words like 'appeared' and 'in' that introduce the periodical where a work was published.
modes.example: and the Colored American Magazine,” which appeared<< in>> American Periodicals.

modes.label: Inside periodical titles
modes.description: A word within a journal title, just before the word Quarterly.

card.writes: It lowers the odds of words like authors, paper, doi and Conference, so the text does not continue as a paper reference.
card.plain: It marks the spot in a reference where the journal or publisher name is about to appear.
